scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that worthy goals can justify hard means, then argues they cannot justify cruelty or injustice; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose at about 400 words on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: People sometimes excuse terrible actions by claiming they served a noble cause.
Some people argue that if a goal is worthy, then any means taken to attain it are justifiable.
I strongly disagree, because even the worthiest goal cannot justify every action, and cruel means often destroy the good they claim to serve.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why worthy goals justify some hard means

sentences.text: First, it is true that good goals sometimes require difficult or unpleasant means.
Achieving something valuable often demands sacrifice, hard choices, and actions that are far from comfortable.
For example, a doctor may cause a patient real pain during surgery in order to save her life.
This shows that a worthy goal can indeed justify means that would otherwise seem harsh.
Soldiers defending their country, too, may have to do hard things for the sake of protecting others.
In such cases, the value of the goal really does help to justify the difficult means used.
To this extent, worthy goals can excuse some otherwise unwelcome actions.
Second, however, the claim that any means are justified goes dangerously too far.
Some actions, such as cruelty, deceit, or harming the innocent, are wrong no matter what goal they serve.
Consider rulers who have killed and oppressed millions while insisting they were building a better world.
Such crimes show that evil means often poison the very goal they were meant to achieve.
A society built through cruelty rarely becomes the just and happy place its leaders promised.
Allowing any means also removes every limit, letting people excuse almost any horror in the name of a cause.
Worthy goals, then, must be pursued through means that are themselves acceptable.
In conclusion, a good goal can justify some difficult and unpleasant means.
But it can never justify cruelty or injustice, which corrupt the cause they claim to serve.
The end alone is not enough, because how we act matters as much as what we are trying to achieve.
